description: geothermal: Rn-222 vented with non-condensable gas per GW a of geothermal electricity, default for countries without own factor; applies to the flash/liquid-dominated rest of the world
notes: REVISION D65 (Steve, 2026-11-04): low 2e+13 -> 5e+12 Bq/GWa (20 -> 5 TBq/(GW a)); central 8e+13 and high 4e+14 unchanged (round-3 P4 option A, research/other/papers_round3.md section 4). Evidence: Kruger, Stoker and Umana 1977 (S1415, Stanford lab, independent) Salton Sea flashing-brine separated steam 3.8 nCi/L x assumed 6-12 kg steam/kWh = 7-15 TBq/(GW a), and Geysers 16.7 nCi/L x 10 kg/kWh = 54; Salton Sea wellhead 1.4 nCi/L is lower still; low 5 sits below the Salton Sea estimate and allows binary and liquid-dominated plants. The NZ estimate 40-200 (S1402, CO2-scaled) is independent but hinges on the assumed 29-150 t CO2/GWh. Larderello provenance chain: every Larderello radon number in the registry traces to D'Amore's 1976 wellhead survey (S1418); the 150 UNSCEAR default is the mean of Larderello and Geysers values, both upstream of that survey and of Anspaugh and Hahn 1979 (S1416), so it is not independent evidence for the rest of the world. Implied world mean (2020 weights, 6.4% ITA 260, 19.3% USA about 45, 74.3% here) about 85 TBq/(GW a), 0.57 of UNSCEAR 150, inside the factor-3 test. The lower option B centre 4e+13 (world mean 55, 0.37) was not adopted. REVISION D61 (Steve, 2026-10-27): central 1.5e+14 -> 8e+13 Bq/GWa (150 -> 80 TBq/(GW a)), low 2e+13 and high 4e+14 unchanged (P1, research/other/papers_round2_geothermal.md section 10). Because ITA and USA have own rows, this row serves only the flash/liquid-dominated rest of the world. Independent NZ flash estimate 40-200, centre 80 TBq/(GW a): Whitehead 1980 stack Rn per L CO2 (S1402 p.283) x assumed 29-150 t CO2/GWh (S1413 lifecycle intensity as the floor), independence I, confidence low-medium. Implied world mean about 83 TBq/(GW a) (2020 weights, 6.4% ITA, 19.3% USA, 74.3% here), ratio 0.56 to UNSCEAR 150, inside the factor-3 test. Choice 1 (ITA 260 / USA 38.5 overrides with a world default) approved. Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): activity is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. The superseded centre 150 TBq/(GW a) was the UNSCEAR adopted value (1988, 1993, 2016), the mean of Larderello 260 and The Geysers 38.5 (two vapour-dominated fields, 1970s-80s); it remains the UNSCEAR convention for benchmark B1. Low 20 and high 400 are the Phase 1 proposal (research/other/notes.md 2.1): 400 is the UNSCEAR 1982 value; 20 allows binary (closed-loop, no venting; inference) and liquid-dominated plants. Wairakei steam Rn-222 averages 630 Bq/L, similar to The Geysers 620 (S0502 Table 4), but Wairakei bores vary over four orders of magnitude (S1402), so a single steam value is not meaningful. The 40x lower Cerro Prieto and Wairakei figure in S0505 is a per-unit-volume reservoir concentration consistent with the steam/liquid density ratio, not a per-kg-steam or per-GW a ratio. Imperial Valley hot-water fluid is 1.1 Bq/L (S0502 Table 4). Extrapolation from two fields to the world fleet; no plant-level data for Iceland, NZ, Turkey, Indonesia, Philippines, Kenya, Mexico. Country rows (ITA, USA) override this row. Not exhalation from residues.

description: geothermal: Rn-222 vented with non-condensable gas per GW a, Italy (Larderello and Tuscan vapour-dominated fields)
notes: REVISION D65 (Steve, 2026-11-04): evidence text only, values unchanged (1e+14 / 2.6e+14 / 4e+14) (round-3 P1). REVISION D61 (Steve, 2026-10-27): no value change (P3). Choice 1 approved: ITA 260 override kept. Added evidence: S0509 Tab. 3 (George et al. 1980, secondary) plant total 8.0 Ci/d over 68,600 t steam/d = 4.3e6 Bq/t steam, 257-286 TBq/(GW a) at 420 MWe and capacity factor 0.9-1.0; Tab. 2 (22 Serrazzano wells) mean 134 nCi/kg = 5.0e6 Bq/t; per-plant range 1.4e6-7.6e6 Bq/t (about 92-500 TBq/(GW a)); low 1e14 and high 4e14 bracket these. All Larderello routes derive from one dataset, D'Amore's wellhead survey of March-June 1976, 193 wells (S1418). George et al. 1980 Table 1 (S1404, LBL-11555 p.7) is stated to come from that earlier study; S0509 Tab. 3 copies George verbatim; UNSCEAR 300 GBq/d is numerically George's 8.0 Ci/d (296 GBq/d). No Larderello number held is independent of the others (tag D). The only separate dataset is the Stanford lab method (Kruger, Stoker and Umana 1977, S1415; Semprini et al. 1982, S1405), 1.4-2.8 times lower than the field method for the same wells (Larderello mean 34.6 nCi/L x 6.8 t steam/MWh = 76 TBq/(GW a)); the low bound 1e+14 (100) is roughly that Stanford-method value and is thereby justified, the central 260 is the field-method value. Later Italian units use less steam per MWh, which could lower the value. Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): activity is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. UNSCEAR 2016 para 157: Larderello 300 GBq/d at about 420 MW = 260 TBq/(GW a). Independent routes: George et al. 1980 as cited in S0509, 8 Ci/d = 108 TBq/a (active plants 1980); RSE 2013 model 9.5e3 Bq/s per MW = 300 TBq/(GW a) (modelled). High 400 = UNSCEAR 1982 world value; low 100 allows lower-radon fields (Amiata, Radicondoli; no data, inference). Applied 1913-2025 although the measurements date from the 1970s-80s. Country generation rows exist only from 1980; earlier years use the world row.

description: geothermal: Rn-222 vented with non-condensable gas per GW a, United States (The Geysers value applied to US geothermal generation)
notes: REVISION D65 (Steve, 2026-11-04): evidence text only, values unchanged (5e+12 / 3.85e+13 / 1.5e+14); the earlier note that 38.5 "may be high" is withdrawn (round-3 P2, P3). REVISION D61 (Steve, 2026-10-27): no value change (P4). Choice 1 approved: USA 38.5 override kept. Evidence: Anspaugh and Hahn 1979 (S1416) Geysers measured Rn-222 1.4 Ci/d at 502 MWe = 18.9 TBq/a = 37.7 TBq/(GW a) (UNSCEAR source, dependent); Kruger, Stoker and Umana 1977 (S1415, independent) 16.7 nCi/L at 10 kg steam/kWh = 54 TBq/(GW a) (43 at 8 kg/kWh). The two bracket 38.5 (geometric mean 45). Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): activity is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. UNSCEAR 2016: The Geysers 38.5 TBq/(GW a) (19.3-21 TBq/a at 502 MW, 1970s-1980). The Geysers is roughly half of US geothermal output; Salton Sea steam is 110 Bq/L, Imperial Valley hot-water fluid 1.1 Bq/L (S0502 Table 4), binary plants vent nothing (inference), so the Geysers value is a central, not a bound. Low 5 TBq/(GW a) allows a large flash/binary share; high 150 = world default centre. Applied from 1960 (first Geysers unit).

description: geothermal: Mass of scale and sludge generated per GW a of geothermal electricity, tonnes (documentation row: the stream script forms mass = GW a x this factor, then applies the Bq/t rows)
notes: REVISION D65 (Steve, 2026-11-04): high 6.1e+4 -> 2.6e+5 t/(GW a); low 1 and centre 250 unchanged (round-3 oil_gas section 8, EPA 1993 B.8 via S1250/S1257 as cited there). Second high-side point: Imperial Valley (hypersaline flash/binary) filter cake about 20,000 m3/a x 1.75 t/m3 = 3.5e4 t/a over about 190 MW listed (1987) at an assumed capacity factor 0.7 = about 2.6e+5 t/(GW a), above the Rockwell 1982 value. Wet cake; single EIR (ERC 1990, not obtained), hypersaline field only; confidence low. WEAKEST FACTOR IN THE FILE. High = Rockwell 1982 hypothetical 100 MWe Salton Sea hypersaline plant, scale 4,500 t/a at 6,500 h/a: 4,500 / (0.1 GW x 6,500/8,766 a) = 6.1e4 t/(GW a) (brine precipitate 16,000 t/a is a separate stream and is not included). The same report says vapour-dominated generation makes 'relatively small quantities of solid wastes' and gives no figure; the low of 1 t/(GW a) is MY ASSUMPTION, not a source. Centre = geometric mean (coal notes rule 6). No measured mass for Larderello, Iceland, Turkey or Kenya was found. Unit t/GWa cannot go through lib apply(); the script multiplies Bounds directly with lib product.

description: biomass_peat+biomass_domestic: Activity per tonne of peat ash from energy peat, U238+
notes: REVISION D65 (Steve, 2026-11-04): low 1.2e+5 -> 5e+4, central 4e+5 -> 2.5e+5 Bq/t; high 4.5e+6 unchanged (round-3 P6). Finnish production peat U-238 4.9 Bq/kg / 0.05 = 98 Bq/kg ash (STUK-A143) and peat-dominated plant fly ash U-238 85 Bq/kg (S1409) lay below the old low; Swedish evidence stays 268-1,048 (Hedvall alpha), median 420 (SSI). 2.5e+5 is about the geometric mean of 420 and about 100, weighted towards Sweden. Ireland, Russia, Belarus and the Baltics unmeasured. Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): activity is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Bulk ash, before stack loss, per tonne of ash (sources in Bq/kg, x1000). Peat activity is the ash value divided by the concentration factor 20 (SSI). Evidence: SSI 2003:02: median of 146 Swedish energy-peat bogs 420 (mean 865, max 9,260); P95 reference 'high-active' ash 4,500; Hedvall 268-1,048; Finland fly ash (Mustonen 1984) 160; Finland peat mean 11 Bq/kg x 20 = 220; UNSCEAR 1988 peat 40 Bq/kg x 20 = 800 (S0008). description: biomass_peat+biomass_domestic: Share of fuel Cs-137 leaving the stack from biomass or peat plants (power, heat, industrial boilers; after filters)
notes: REVISION D65 (Steve, 2026-11-04): high 0.05 -> 0.13; low 0.0005 and central 0.005 unchanged (round-3 P5). Hedvall and Erlandsson 1992 (S1419) Sandviken peat plant mass balance: particulate stack escape 0.66% (supports the central); 12 +/- 2% unaccounted, assumed gaseous by the authors (upper bound 0.12-0.13); the gap is within the peat-input scatter (CV 14%), so it may be sampling error. Only one primary mass balance exists. REVISION D61 (Steve, 2026-10-27): no value change (P8). Pepin et al. 2023 (S0513 p.759-764) supports near-complete capture of fuel Cs-137 in plant ash (Belgian plant ash about 200 Bq/kg; Austrian pellet ash 195-867; concentration factor wood to ash 100-200, i.e. CF x ash fraction about 0.5-1). No stack measurement. Two routes: (i) volatilised fraction 0.10 (assumption, S0515/S0536) x (1 - dust control 0.99, UNSCEAR 1988 peat assumption in S0519) = 1e-3; (ii) escaping ash fraction 0.01 x fine-fraction enrichment 4.5 (Po-210 analogue) = 4.5e-2. Centre sits between them; the Fukushima forestry-waste incinerator with a wet scrubber found no gaseous Cs (S0551). Applies to wood and peat Cs-137 in plants (script selects by driver_series wood_fuel_t).

description: biomass_domestic: Share of fuel Cs-137 leaving as stove or chimney emission, household wood and peat
notes: REVISION D65 (Steve, 2026-11-04): evidence text replaced, value unchanged (0.05 / 0.19 / 0.7) (round-3 P8). REVISION D61 (Steve, 2026-10-27): central 0.25 -> 0.19 (choice 4 and P7), the geometric mean of the bounds sqrt(0.05 x 0.70) = 0.187; low 0.05 and high 0.70 unchanged. The Phase 1 centre 0.25-0.30 was mid-range, not evidence-weighted. No upper bound on release can be drawn from ash retention. The wood-to-ash factor 50 is an unsupported IAEA default (S1408, TECDOC-1376 pp.32, 38, 55). Measured paired factors (Grill 2021, S1411): pellets 88-580 (mean 228), chips 24-99 (mean 61); with ash yields 0.5% (pellets) and 1% (chips) ash retention is about 1.1 (0.44-2.9) and 0.6 (0.25-1.0), so the earlier "at most 0.4-0.45 leaves" bound does not hold. Pellet appliances look close to full retention, which supports the low bound 0.05 for pellets. Pepin gives no stove emission measurement. Pepin gives no stove emission measurement. Phase 1 proposal (household notes 2.3): low 0.05, high 0.70, centre 0.25-0.30 (mid-range, not evidence-weighted); the geometric mean of the bounds is 0.19, now adopted as the centre. Direct domestic points: Sweden about 0 (K-40 ratio, unpaired), Japan firewood about 0.09 and charcoal 0.10-0.16 (S0564, derived), Greece 0.41-0.79 (indirect, S0531), lab cedar bark 0.15-0.35 at 350-500 C (S0551), lab 'typical field fire' 0.40-0.70 (S0549), open fire 0.0008-0.0045 (S0552, not transferable). The 0.10 in Task 1.6 is an assumption (S0515 'a fairly free assumption'). No stove stack measurement exists. Applied also to household peat.

notes: Japan Forestry Agency slide: charcoal ash 30 g/kg and concentration factor 28 against full retention 33, i.e. 84-90% of radiocaesium stays in the ash, 0.10-0.16 to the air (derived, not stated in the source). Low and high widened for the single-source basis. No radionuclide measurement of charcoal exists.

description: geothermal: Rn-220 released per Rn-222 released with non-condensable gas (unit-1 ratio to the Rn-222 flow of the same plant), all countries
notes: REVISION D61 (Steve, 2026-10-27): NEW ROW (choice 2 superseded by P5). Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): activity is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Applied as the Rn-222 head flow (other:0001-0003) times this ratio, tier liberated, route air_vented_gas, group Rn220+. Evidence: Whitehead and Ditchburn 1996 (S0508) Table 1 p.319, 22 wells (20 Wairakei, 2 Ohaaki) plus 1 fumarole, wellhead Rn-220/Rn-222 geometric mean 0.34, median 0.47, ratio of sums 0.20, range 0.02-3.5 (fumarole 1.34). Rn-220 half-life 55.6 s, so survival to the stack is 2^(-t/55.6): 0.47 at 60 s, 0.22 at 120 s, 0.024 at 300 s; assumed transit 1-5 min (inference, not in the paper) gives stack ratio about 0.34 x (0.02-0.47) = 0.01-0.16. High 0.35 = no decay (wellhead GM); low 0.005 = long transit and low-ratio wells; centre 0.05. Implied Rn-220 about 4e12 Bq/GWa (XWL) and 1.3e13 (ITA). Wellhead confidence medium, stack confidence low. Pb-212 ingrowth is a separate engine question. Whitehead 1980 (S1402) detected no Rn-220 and gave no figures. Not exhalation from residues.

description: geothermal: Rn-222 vented with non-condensable gas per GW a, New Zealand (Wairakei, Ohaaki and other liquid-dominated flash fields)
notes: REVISION D61 (Steve, 2026-10-27): NEW ROW (P2). Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): activity is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Basis recorded as modelled because "derived" is not in the basis vocabulary. Whitehead 1980 (S1402 p.283) Wairakei stack mean 8.23 nCi/L CO2 (gas entering the station about 12 nCi/L) = 1.5e8-2.4e8 Bq per t CO2, times an assumed 29-150 t CO2/GWh (S1413 lifecycle intensity 29 g CO2e/kWh at Wairakei 2021-22 as the floor; 1970s intensity probably higher) times 8766 GWh/(GW a) = 4e13-2e14 Bq/(GW a), centre about 8e13. High 3e14 includes the 4x higher Robertson-column reading (mean 37 nCi/L CO2; Whitehead internal inconsistency unresolved). Independent of UNSCEAR 2016 (tag I). Confidence low. NZ is about 8% of world geothermal generation (7,728 of 95,098 GWh, 2020, S0510), so this row mostly documents; P1 carries the weight. Country generation rows start 1980; earlier years use the XWL row.
